title: Discover installed capabilities and operations
summary: List every installed capability and operation with enough meaning for an agent to select plausible contracts, then read their full operating boundaries.
use_when: A request may map to an installed local capability or adaptive operation.
The exact supported outcome, effects, authority, recovery, privacy, or invocation must be understood without inspecting source code.
do_not_use_when: The correct capability is already known and its current contract has already been read in this session.
The task is ordinary work with no plausible installed-system catalog need.
outcome: The caller receives a complete semantic catalog or one complete installed contract; no represented action is performed.
effects: Reads explicitly indexed JSON and Markdown from installed provider bundles.
Writes no provider state and performs no readiness probe.
authority: Provider bundles are authoritative for documented support and semantics.
Chancery is authoritative only for structural validation, installed catalog discovery, and presentation.
The represented product remains authoritative for runtime readiness and domain success.
success: List reports every structurally valid installed entry, including deprecated or dependency-unavailable entries, with visible registry issues.
Show returns the complete version-matched contract and manual for an installed entry.
No documented invocation is executed as a side effect of discovery.
failure_and_recovery: A malformed provider is excluded and reported without hiding structurally valid providers.
A missing or incompatible dependency makes the affected entry unavailable until the owning provider is installed or updated.
Use doctor to inspect registry structure; use the provider's own operating contract for live readiness.
privacy: Installed documentation is processed locally and is not retained by Chancery.
Chancery has no network or model integration.

consumers.statement: Interactive agents and local readers that need the installed catalog or one exact product-owned contract may use this read-only capability.

preconditions.statement: The selected registry directory exists, and product installers have published any provider selectors the caller expects to discover.

inputs.statement: List accepts optional mode and kind filters; show accepts one exact stable entry ID.
Natural-language request text is not an input to Chancery and is not matched or ranked by this capability.

outputs.statement: List emits catalog cards and registry issues; show emits the selected provider identity, complete entry document, dependency statuses, manual, availability, compatibility, readiness classification, and registry issues.

data_semantics.statement: Support is provider-declared, availability means the installed bundle is structurally valid, compatibility concerns documentation-contract dependencies, and readiness is never established by discovery.

identity_and_units.statement: Provider ID, provider release, stable entry ID, entry contract version, and provider schema version are distinct identities and versions.
Discovery publishes no domain measurement or quantitative unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: List is complete for every explicitly indexed entry in every structurally valid provider fixed during that invocation; invalid providers and registry issues remain visible.
Each invocation rereads the selected installed registry and retains no earlier catalog snapshot.
Catalog completeness does not mean every possible product behavior has been published or that represented runtimes are currently ready.

access.statement: Access is a local read of an absolute registry path or the current user's default Chancery registry; indexed inner symlinks and path escapes are rejected.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: One invocation canonicalizes each selector once, constructs one deterministic in-memory view, prints it, and exits without writing provider or registry state.
A malformed provider is excluded as a unit, duplicate global entry IDs are excluded rather than selected by filesystem order, and dependency unavailability propagates transitively.

operational_limits.statement: Configured bounds limit provider count, entries per provider, manifest and entry size, manual size, and individual field size.
No wall-clock discovery latency or registry-size service-level objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: This reader accepts provider schemas 1, 2, and 3; removed schema-1 routing metadata is ignored only for schema 1, and unknown fields remain errors.
No retirement date is promised here for legacy provider schema support.

reliances.statement: Discovery creates no runtime, data, authority, or readiness reliance on a represented product; installed provider documentation is its local input.
